newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks end lower, PC shrs hit by rumours.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks end lower, PC shrs hit by rumours.

text.p: Stocks closed a touch lower on Wednesday as profit taking emerged after a rise of six consecutive trading days, brokers said.

"Consolidation was expected. But overall sentiment continues to run strong due to abundant money supply," said Chang Keun-ho of Daishin Securities. The composite index provisionally closed 0.93 of a point lower at 712.50.
Shares of computer makers plunged on rumours of financial trouble stemming from sluggish personal computer (PC) sales.
Trigem Computer fell 2,200 won to its daily limit of 25,800 and ALEX dropped 3,500 won to 41,200.
Officials at the companies said the rumours about financial problems were groundless.
Daewoo Telecom also fell 560 won to 8,440. It briefly hit its lower limit of 8,280 won.

Volume totalled 35.26 million shares, compared with 41.37 million on Tuesday. Decliners outpaced advancers 522 to 289 with 102 unchanged. Mining firms continued to pick up after Tuesday's news that a mining area would be developed into a resort town.
Coal miner Dong Won rose 4,100 won to its daily limit of 56,500, and Daesung also went limit-up, climbing 8,500 won to 115,500.
Brokers said customer deposits with securities houses rose to three trillion won from about 2.95 trillion won last week.
They forecast trading would be firmer on Thursday after today's correction.
Less-than-expected new stock issues this month and in March, including rights issues and initial public offerings, would help support sentiment.
Such issues were estimated at 45 billion won in February, against 150 billion in January.
The March futures contracts fell 0.1 of a point to 73.20, while the KOSPI 200 index declined 0.02 of a point to 74.62.
